events.quote: On May 20, 2026, Ford's Recall Service Program (RSP) team introduced a concern to Ford's Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) after an RSP Analyst identified a vehicle that had Field Service Action (FSA) 26C10 marked as complete

Subsequent investigation determined that although the vehicle had successfully received the FSA 26C10 software update, the commercially available Ford ITRM accessory kit contains ITRM modules with obsoleted pre-FSA 26C10 software.

The ITRM accessory kit installation instructions did not direct the dealer to perform an ITRM software update as part of the installation, thereby reintroducing the software condition previously addressed by FSA 26C10.
On May 20, 2026, Ford initiated containment actions to prevent further distribution of affected inventory for all Ford ITRM accessory kits containing the software level recalled under 26C10.
Between May 20, 2026, and June 25, 2026, Ford's cross-functional team investigated the affected population.

Of the sold population, 315 kits were installed on vehicles and traced to specific VINs outside the 26C10 population, while the remaining 1,043 units represented over-the-counter or online sales for which a documented transaction existed but could not be linked to a specific VIN.

On June 25, 2026, Ford's Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) completed its investigation, which considered Ford’s 26C10 recall and Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, Section 6.2.1.

Based on this review, and because the ITRM accessory kits contain the same software previously recalled under 26C10, CCRG recommended an equipment recall for the ITRM accessory kits sold containing the software level identified under 26C10.
On July 7, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved a field action.

events_excluded.sentence: As of June 25, 2026, this team accounted for a total population of 3,157 ITRM accessory kits, comprised of 1,799 kits held in inventory and 1,358 kits sold.
As of June 25, 2026, no warranty claims or Vehicle Owner Questionnaires (VOQs) have been identified as potentially related to this condition.
Ford is not aware of any reports of accident or injury related to this condition.

cause.label: cause stated
cause.quote: A software vulnerability within the ITRM allows for a potential race condition to occur between the ITRM and the CAN Standby Control bit (STBCC) during initial power-up.

events.quote: On December 22, 2025, the Kentucky Truck Plant (KTP) Plant Vehicle Team reported that three 2025 model year Super Duty vehicles experienced separation of the aluminum driveshaft during End-of-Line testing.
The separation occurred at the friction weld between the driveshaft tube and driveshaft end yoke.
KTP issued a stop ship for this concern on the same day.
Ford and the supplier conducted testing on the welders used to produce the subject driveshafts on December 22, 2025.
The supplier uses two friction welders for aluminum driveshaft tube friction welding.
All three separated driveshafts were produced on the same welder.
Testing confirmed that the issue was isolated to driveshafts produced on only one of the two welders, due to degradation of that welder’s spindle.
On January 8, 2026, this issue was brought to Ford’s Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) for review.

During the CCRG’s investigation, Ford and the supplier reviewed supplier production history and analyzed weld quality data to determine the population of driveshafts that may not have sufficient weld penetration to prevent a separation.
Ford utilized this information to determine suspect vehicle production.
These reports were received between January 14, 2026, and February 24, 2026, and represent six unique VINs.
On February 24, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved a field action.

events_excluded.sentence: As of February 24, 2026, Ford is aware of six warranty claims and five field reports for driveshaft separation.
Ford is not aware of any accidents, fires or injuries related to this concern.

cause.label: cause stated
cause.quote: Due to degradation, the spindle at the friction weld station did not reach sufficient speed to provide acceptable weld energy.

To support this request and given the passage of time, beginning in early December 2025, OEV undertook a comprehensive review of the training seat and its compliance with any applicable FMVSS requirements.
The review included an assessment of whether or not the training seat qualified as a Designated Seating Position under 49 C.F.R.
§ 571.3, whether the specialized orientation of the training seat qualified it as a side-facing seat, and an assessment of whether the training seat met associated performance requirements.
This assessment occurred through early March 2026, and on March 6, 2026, OEV concluded that the training seat did not meet FMVSS requirements for Designated Seating Positions under FMVSS 207 and 210.

events_excluded.sentence: OEV is not aware of any deaths or injuries potentially related to this issue.

events.quote: On January 14, 2026, Hino discovered during a Model Year 2027 production audit that some owner’s manuals for the identified Model Year 2026 vehicles contained pages from an owner’s manual associated with a different vehicle model.
Hino worked with the supplier to investigate the issue and identify the root cause and potential scope.
Hino also began to assess potential customer impacts that could result from the issue.

In February 2026, the supplier reported to Hino that a printer malfunction occurred while printing a specific order and, when printing resumed, the incorrect inside pages were mistakenly selected and printed for the remainder of the order.
Hino reviewed production records to identify the population of vehicles for which the incorrect owner’s manual may have been provided.

Hino also identified several differences between the correct and incorrect manual pages that could result in safety concerns in the event owners rely on the information in performing certain maintenance.
A technical review was performed to evaluate the impact those differences could have on vehicle safety.
In March 2026, Hino concluded that the front U-Bolt tightening torque specification in the incorrect pages was higher than the correct specification, which could result in bolt breakage if followed.
On March 17, 2026, based on the investigation results, Hino determined to conduct a voluntary safety recall campaign for the subject vehicles.

events_excluded.sentence: As of March 16, 2026, Hino is not aware of warranty claims related to the issue.
Hino is also not aware of reports of injuries or accidents related to the issue.
